findings.title: Direct share unmasking can publish a different phrase from the wallet-checked revision
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The supported wallet-verification result or mandatory regression gate is incorrect; resolve and verify before release.
findings.reproduction: Run share-boundaries.mjs. Restore the public 2-of-3 fixture, shallow-copy its genuine RepairedSet metadata, enter a gated truthful wallet callback, change only the host object mnemonic, then release the callback.
findings.expected: A successful recovery and candidate list contain the exact phrase checked, or reject stale input.
findings.observed: checkedOriginal=true; publishedOriginal=false; publishedUncheckedReplacement=true; listedUncheckedReplacement=true. Immutable matching and nonmatching controls pass.
findings.impact: A supported mutable structural input can race an awaited wallet check. Normal frozen ShareSet inputs limit exposure; no ordinary CLI misrecovery, collision, funds loss or dishonest callback was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Snapshot the input collection and each set/phrase before the first await; verify and publish that owned revision through the common unmasking owner.
findings.requiredVerification: Gated set and collection mutation; true/false wallet controls; direct and whole-date/partial-date controls; metadata coherence and existing cancellation tests.

findings.title: Separate-card regressions still require a sheet-font planning path
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The supported wallet-verification result or mandatory regression gate is incorrect; resolve and verify before release.
findings.reproduction: Run retained-export-dispatch, or the existing allows a failed library plan to be retried test alone. Its arguments request business-sized individual cards and exporters are passive mocks.
findings.expected: Count-only individual plans require no font reads; a failed sheet-planning regression deliberately reaches its injected failing service.
findings.observed: Eight test failures: fontReads is 0 while assertions require 1 or 2. Code and retained-plan assertions before these counters pass; the intended font-failure/retry path is never entered.
findings.impact: Mandatory regression acceptance is red and the stated retry coverage is absent. This does not demonstrate lost codes or a broken production retry owner.
findings.recommendedFix: Retain zero-font individual planning. Correct its assertions and choose an actual sheet plan for the existing font-failure/retry test; keep renderers passive.
findings.requiredVerification: The complete affected file, targeted failure/retry controls and the current individual-card count checks without generating PDF.

findings.title: Metadata regression transfers the same renderer-owned PDF buffer twice
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The supported wallet-verification result or mandatory regression gate is incorrect; resolve and verify before release.
findings.reproduction: Static alias proof: the metadata test mock always returns one bytes array; first renderCards stores it in pages and wipes that array in finally; the later exportCards reuses the same jobs and array. The PDF-generating test was not executed.
findings.expected: Each mock invocation transfers a fresh valid owned document, while an independent original stays available as an oracle.
findings.observed: The second transfer supplies the previously zeroed buffer. The exact first runtime failure is unmeasured; an earlier parsed original may also retain byte views.
findings.impact: The mandatory metadata/content regression cannot establish both preview and saved output as written. Correct production cleanup is not a product regression.
findings.recommendedFix: Return an independent owned copy per mock invocation and preserve the original oracle. Keep renderer-owned buffer wiping.
findings.requiredVerification: When PDF execution is authorized, run preserves page content and removes private metadata in preview and saved PDFs, plus nearby ownership and metadata checks.

findings.title: Two table regressions test rejected Promises with synchronous toThrow
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The supported wallet-verification result or mandatory regression gate is incorrect; resolve and verify before release.
findings.reproduction: Run the five precisely filtered cases in stale-contract-regressions, or cli-boundaries.mjs. Both affected tests call expect(() => runTable(...)).toThrow after runTable became async.
findings.expected: Await the rejected Promise and assert the stable input-refusal contract.
findings.observed: Both assertions fail with expected [Function] to throw an error. Vitest records two unhandled rejections, code cli.arguments.base-10-integer-from. The direct probe confirms a coded Promise rejection and no synchronous throw.

findings.recommendedFix: Use awaited rejects assertions and audit all callers of the changed asynchronous handler; preserve the coded refusal.
findings.requiredVerification: The two exact cases, rejection handling and normal table lookup/export tests, with no full PDF/PNG suite.

findings.title: Screen-only large share sets overflow the finite private terminal without a revisit path
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Run terminal-frames.py against the recorded Linux executable, 80 columns by 24 rows. Encode public abandon x11/about as 16-of-16 word shares, screen only, backup check no. Inspect the current bounded VT frame before clearing, then send Up/PageUp.
findings.expected: Every screen-only backup share remains accessible until the person finishes copying or checking it.
findings.observed: Transcript contains all 16 share titles, but the finite current frame contains only titles 11 through 16. Share 1 remains absent after Up/PageUp; the application offers no paging/revisit action.
findings.impact: Incomplete visible output for this supported finite terminal configuration. The source phrase remains available and file export is a workaround. This is not a claim about all emulator/multiplexer scrollback policies.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a shared row-aware private-result presenter with next/previous or replay and preserved stdout behavior; reuse it for all multiline secret results.
findings.requiredVerification: Finite 80x24 and narrow/large frames, all share forms and small/large quorums, keyboard back/next, result/check retention and redirected complete output.

findings.title: Dropped POSIX paths with embedded apostrophes are decoded incorrectly
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Run cli-boundaries.mjs: encode the synthetic literal ./it's.txt with the repository POSIX quoting producer, then pass that spelling into droppedPath.
findings.expected: Supported dragged/quoted path normalization restores the literal filename without evaluating a shell.
findings.observed: The apostrophe round trip is false; raw literal and ordinary quoted-space controls pass. The decoder only strips the exterior quotes and retains inner quoted/escaped segments.
findings.impact: Some legal dropped filenames fail to read; typing the literal path is a workaround. No shell execution or injection was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Use one deliberately small, documented argument-quoting grammar shared by the producer/reader as appropriate; never eval or execute a shell to decode a path.
findings.requiredVerification: Literal and dropped spellings with spaces, apostrophes, backslashes, dollar/backtick characters, Unicode, local URLs and platform controls.

findings.title: The POSIX PTY test driver leaves its master descriptor open
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Run terminal-frames.py. Start one text-only table lookup, wait for exit, call Session.close, then os.fstat the PTY master. The audit probe closes its own descriptor afterwards.
findings.expected: An idempotent Session.close releases the owned master descriptor and reaps its child.
findings.observed: os.fstat succeeds after close: descriptorClosed=false. No os.close or owning file wrapper exists in the driver.
findings.impact: One descriptor leaks per completed session until interpreter exit. Ordinary scripts have finite counts; no product secret leak or host exhaustion was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Own and close the PTY descriptor once in an idempotent lifetime; preserve child cleanup and Windows behavior.
findings.requiredVerification: Normal exit, repeated close, cancellation/start failure, no descriptor accumulation and no orphaned children.

findings.title: A mixed-share test assumes two random splits have different protocol identifiers
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Run identifier-precondition.mjs. Real ShareSplit with distinct public seeds produces different payloads; rewrite only set B's 16-bit identifier by walking the actual CBOR header and updating CRC. Require A, B and rewritten B own quorums to restore the public phrase; compare equal-ID mixed metadata preflight with unchanged different-ID rejection. No random collision loop.
findings.expected: A deterministic negative fixture explicitly has different identifiers, rather than depending on independent random calls to produce different values.
findings.observed: All three own-quorum controls restore. The distinct-ID control is refused; both equal-ID mixed metadata preflights return undefined despite different payloads. The original random test establishes no distinct-identifier precondition. No spontaneous OS-random failure was observed.
findings.impact: A permitted random identifier collision can make the test flaky. This does not establish incorrect production reconstruction: digest/entropy checks are separate from metadata preflight.
findings.recommendedFix: Use fixed public sets with explicitly different identifiers for the negative case; keep a separate production-CSPRNG contract test and a colliding-identifier control.
findings.requiredVerification: Deterministic different-ID negative and same-ID metadata controls, without looping until an OS-random collision appears.

findings.title: Curated release notes retain the obsolete separate-card decoy count
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Compare the release paragraph with the current shared count rule and the passing 24-word Unicode planning regression. No rendering is needed.
findings.expected: Separate cards retain exactly one extra code; collection sheets fill their rows.
findings.observed: The release note says separate cards receive as many extras as the sheet and all layouts show the same cards. Current plan gives 25 separate cards for 24 Unicode codes versus the 28-card sheet fixture.
findings.impact: Incorrect future release guidance; no altered backup bytes or recovery failure. The format numbers in the same notes remain correct.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the curated paragraph from current CHANGELOG/design documentation before publication.
findings.requiredVerification: Static prose/rule comparison and the existing plan-only count test.

findings.title: Shared image-format help implies PNG for separate files that default to PDF
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Run cli-boundaries.mjs or compare encode help with cardFileFormat({}) and imageFormat({}); no rendering is involved.
findings.expected: Help distinguishes the PDF default of separate card files from the PNG default of page images.
findings.observed: The summary says Image format for --images-dir and --cards-dir; default png. The actual defaults are cardDefault=pdf and pageImageDefault=png.
findings.impact: A user can expect the wrong file type. The implementation default itself is intentional and unchanged.
findings.recommendedFix: Build the summary from the existing canonical default constants and describe each destination precisely.
findings.requiredVerification: Help text versus both default functions and explicit png/jpg choices.

findings.title: Successful SSKR recovery frees its WASM output without wiping the mutable intermediate
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Run wasm-output.mjs. Initialize the pinned unmodified WASM, recover one public 32-byte fixture, verify and zero the returned JS array. Re-enter only the retained 16-byte return frame to identify the freed output allocation; do not allocate another WASM value.
findings.expected: After copying output into its returned JS owner, zero the owned mutable WASM allocation before releasing it.
findings.observed: The actual output frame reports pointer 1254208 and length 32; all 32 bytes still match the public entropy after the JS owner is wiped. The formatted wrapper has the same static copy/free sequence but was not independently executed.
findings.impact: Residual secret lifetime within the same runtime. No network exposure, attacker access, retention duration, whole-heap erasure claim or wallet compromise is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Fix the canonical bridge output transfer/cleanup once, using the build-owned source/transform rather than hand-editing generated files; rebuild and refresh integrity and host pins.
findings.requiredVerification: Public output-allocation controls before reuse, both recovery variants, corresponding create/output paths, caller-owned success output intact, refusals and canonical byte verification at the authorized release stage.

findings.title: Short missing-code candidate lists overflow the private viewport
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no mandatory integrity failure or immediate wallet compromise established.
findings.reproduction: Run terminal-frames.py: decode a public 24-word phrase with its last word marked ?, list candidates, direct mode, finite 80x24 Linux PTY.
findings.expected: The person can access every offered candidate even when its codes and phrase wrap onto several rows.
findings.observed: The first candidate exists in the transcript but not in the finite current frame, before or after Up/PageUp. The presenter bounds candidate count rather than rendered rows and offers no paging.
findings.impact: Some valid candidates cannot be compared in this tested terminal configuration. Redirected output or a narrower search is a workaround. No incorrect candidate or universal emulator limitation is claimed.
findings.recommendedFix: Reuse the same row-aware private-result presentation owner as share output; retain numbering, fingerprints and complete redirected output.
findings.requiredVerification: Eight long 24-word candidates, 16-candidate bound, narrow/large frames, navigation and stdout parity.

informationalObservations: No additional confirmed semantic duplication was found. Keep shared EncodedForm, Masking, topology/algebra, file-publication and render-platform owners. The >=50-token gate is lexical evidence, not semantic proof.

Use one row-aware private-result presenter for both share and missing-code overflow; avoid two separate pagers. A deeper retained phrase CardPlan is optional; do not create a framework or rewrite code merely for style.
G1-001 Bytewords/UR cross-language ownership is explicitly owner-deferred to the later Rust port; it is not reopened or treated as a current release blocker.
Recoloured reference-dependent raster buffers lack an explicit wipe in source, but sensitivity/impact were not validated under the image ban. Keep as an unvalidated observation, not a confirmed leak.

Direct/whole-date ShareUnmasking ignores run.signal, but its documented signal contract specifically names date search. Contract clarification is required before treating it as another cancellation finding.

Additional coverage opportunities: nonzero RGB offset tags, GF(2) free-vector independence, intact companions in repaired CLI export, child exit status for QR readback, same-source dist binding, composed full-set write failures and current full-self-test feature composition.

The joint solver materializes readable representatives from at most eight hidden directions. No concrete omitted phrase was found; nonlinear text-constraint completeness is a proof/coverage gap, not a finding.

Artifact artwork creator/source/license provenance is less explicit than font/map provenance; no unlicensed copying is alleged. Release-attestation identity/expected asset-set checks remain optional hardening, not a demonstrated exploit.
limitations: No PDF painting/saving, raster/PNG/JPEG generation or decoding, full card gallery, pixel comparison, Poppler output or real QR scan was executed. Tiny structural PNG startup byte fixtures are parser checks, not media outputs. Numerical planning and fake renderer bytes do not establish readable exports.

No full test suite, exhaustive entropy-tail/full-cost vector replay, 120-policy SSKR matrix, 6000-comparison oracle, Docker/canonical WASM rebuild or new Rust advisory DB refresh. Selected small published fixtures and ordinary KATs were executed.

Linux native PTY with a finite VT-frame oracle is not a graphical terminal screenshot or proof of all emulator/multiplexer behavior. Current Windows/macOS native artifacts and final-commit CI remain unverified.
External 190-pin/180-test host parity is retained wallet-tools evidence at its own source fingerprint, not AUD-028 browser execution. No actual host browser was driven.

Dependency call integration and locks were reviewed; every upstream/transitive implementation, license and cryptographic primitive was not independently audited. WASM/source equivalence was not newly established.

All current source and 143 current test bodies have primary read attestations; binaries received identity/provenance review and the 381 historical inputs received structural/retained review. Complete enumeration is not universal semantic review or proof every defect was found.

One initial syntax inventory attempt exceeded its reviewer memory target (296956 KiB) despite exit 0. It was superseded by bounded static runs; no product memory failure is alleged. All guarded coordinator product checks stayed below 1 GiB RSS with at least 3 GiB host reserve.

Best-effort cleanup cannot guarantee erasure of immutable JS strings/BigInts, upstream/OS copies, swap, terminal recording or malicious same-process hosts. The narrow confirmed WASM allocation residue is stated separately.

Review only: pre-existing dirty implementation/test/docs changes preserved. No production, fixture, dependency, workflow or canonical generated file was edited, and no commit/push/tag/release was made.
